ContextForge remains the operational transport for configured clients until each consumer/service contract has verified parity and rollback evidence.
Direct Serena in current Pi is an explicit exception and must not be reported as ContextForge-backed.
Service locality follows filesystem, credential, session, and project boundaries; gateway-container hosting is not the default.
No canonical-event ContextForge sink is assumed to exist merely because MCP virtual servers exist.
migration_gates: Inventory every live, recorded, and hidden consumer, including caches, project state, user units, and development harnesses.
Capture tool/prompt/resource names, schemas, error semantics, auth scopes, session behavior, redaction, rate limits, and service locality per attachment.
Pass identical client-visible fixtures through old and proposed paths without widening authority or exposing credentials.
Prove gateway-wide and per-service failure behavior, idempotent retry, state/session continuity, and no hidden fallback.
Provide tested rollback that restores prior config, virtual-server identity, token boundary, and service health without data loss.
Change one independently reviewable service/consumer edge at a time under a separate issue and implementation:QA pair.
